<!-- pr-reviewer: cc00b664f1cfd9b4fdc50106bab49f55feb7da96 -->
**Ready for the maintainer to merge** — K5 (#4178) of the path kernel, `side/path-kernel` (trial merge against `origin/side/path-kernel` 6fb3d55ce: clean, "Already up to date").

Trial base: `origin/side/path-kernel` at 6fb3d55ce (not `main`). Builds and tests ran locally in a fresh worktree off the PR head.

## What looks good

- `Entry::led` is the single gate: the descent is bound to the proof's place, the lead is bound to the room it names, and the lead must start where the descent ends (`proof.rs`, `Lead::new`). Every entry of the crate goes through it.
- The helix and the ramp stay in the legal room and refuse by name (`material.rs`); the exit refuses an unproved lead-out and a retract below the top (`exit.rs`).
- The named fallback carries the stage, the asked and the used names and the reason, and is checked against the law suite (`l4_fallback.rs`).
- Every refusal reason is a named const; `EntryChoice`, `MaterialChoice`, `Heights`, `ArcChoice` and `Hole` refuse bad values at construction.
- The narrowed L4 reading (air entries, holes and columns are not fallbacks when a material entry was asked) matches the pre-existing doc comment in `tests/laws/l4_fallback.rs` — the base code treated `ArcLead` as into-material and contradicted that comment; this PR makes the code agree with it. The decision doc (item 1) names the same reading deliberately.
- The `#[non_exhaustive]` status of the types matches the decision doc (`Proof` deliberately not open; `EntryKind` stays open).
- Process files are untouched; the body starts with `Side branch: side/path-kernel`, ends with `Refs #4178` (not `Fixes #N`), and the decision doc records the shape.

## Results (trial merge with origin/side/path-kernel, 6fb3d55ce)

Local build on the head tree (head tree == base tree after the merge: `git diff cc00b664f^1 cc00b664f` is empty):

- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-geometry --no-run`: built ok
- `cargo test -p camcraft-geometry --lib geo2d::arc`: 4 passed, 0 failed
- `cargo test -p camcraft-pathkernel --test laws`: 88 passed, 0 failed (16 pins of entry_stage and exit + l4_fallback/l5_entry + the rest of the suite)
- `cargo clippy -p camcraft-pathkernel -p camcraft-geometry --all-targets -- -D warnings`: clean
- Light lane (`cargo xtask gate light --base origin/side/path-kernel`): all 7 steps ok, 0 failed — `light build (release --no-run)` 742 s, `motion light: lib` 374 s, `adaptive_troch_island` 45 s, `adaptive_troch_neck` 18 s, `adaptive_troch_parallel` 11 s, `pocket_pass_start` 3 s, `offset_pass_start` 57 s (wall 21.0 min). Logs: `gate-logs/light-20261126-172428`.

The author's gate at the pre-merge head 0daa62a0e (1223 steps, 0 failed; light lane 7 steps, 0 failed) covers this tree exactly; merged with the `cc00b664f` merge commit, the tree is unchanged.

## Targeted tests

- No post or toolpath change: no `example_catalog*` suites of `camcraft-app` needed (nothing in this PR touches `camcraft-app`).
- Light lane: ok (see Results). This PR does not reach a heavy lane; a `P2` PR gets no heavy step.

## Requested before merge

None.

## Questions / notes (not blocking)

- `Exit::new` is a public constructor that cannot check the retract against the material top (only the caller can); the stage always goes through `Exit::proved`. Only test stand-ins call it. Worth a one-line doc line on the constructor saying the caller must check the top — or an `Exit::new` that takes the top. (`crates/pathkernel/src/entry/exit.rs:54-63`)
- The record's L4 line ("An entry where the user asked for another kind is a Fallback", `RECOMMENDED.md` "Stage 6") is now less precise than the code: the asked kind applies only where the tool must enter material, and an arc lead is one family with an air entry (`crates/pathkernel/src/entry/mod.rs:69-78`). The decision doc item 1 says all this; the record may deserve the same one-line touch at the cut.
- The `with_line` fallback in `air.rs` keeps the first straight-lead found and drops the other candidate side; if both sides of the arc fit, the lead is chosen by side order, not by the room that fits. Looks deliberate (the iteration tries ccw true then false) but is worth a glance. (`crates/pathkernel/src/entry/air.rs:62-86`)
- The above-the-top branch builds a conservative `disc(at, ROOM_TOL)` proof over the start point only (`stage.rs:181-185`), which is sound (the descent is a single point) but means the proof can never show a deep in-air descent. Fine for the current consumers; flagging so the K2 consumer knows.
- `Hole::radius()` and `Hole::center()` carry no depth: the caller must give only holes that reach the cut depth (`proof.rs:36-47`). Documented in `mod.rs`; worth a call-site check later.

A maintainer will approve and merge by hand.
